messages.subject: Difference between "regression" (~) and "Manifestation" (=~)
parts:
This may be a stats misunderstanding but I'm confused by the following, when trying to convert a diagram into lavaan model syntax.
 
If I have a simple SEM diagram with edges:
 
A -> L
L -> B
L -> C
 
Where A is my exogenous variable, B and C are observed and L is latent.
 
Then surely I could say
L ~ A
L =~ B + C
 
or surely I could equally say
L ~ A
L =~ B
C ~ L
 
Both of these would seem to correspond equally to the diagram.
 
But these two give me very different solutions.  At first I thought this was because by saying C is regressed on L, I am not constraining the covariance between C and B, but when I look at the solution to the model fit, there is no C~~B residual term, what does appear to be different is that an A~~C link has appeared.  What is happening here and which is the "correct" formula?
 
N = 1000
set.seed(100)
X = rnorm(N)
Y = X + rnorm(N)
df = data.frame(A = X, B = Y + rnorm(N), C = Y + rnorm(N))

simple.sem.1 <- sem("A ~ L\nL =~ B + C", df)

simple.sem.2 <- sem("A ~ L\nL =~ B\nC ~ L  ", df)

standardizedSolution(simple.sem.1)

##   lhs op rhs est.std    se     z pvalue
## 1   A  ~   L   0.754 0.035 21.84      0
## 2   L =~   B   0.782    NA    NA     NA
## 3   L =~   C   0.816 0.037 22.34      0
## 4   B ~~   B   0.389 0.027 14.25      0
## 5   C ~~   C   0.334 0.027 12.22      0
## 6   A ~~   A   0.432 0.027 15.71      0
## 7   L ~~   L   1.000 0.076 13.21      0

standardizedSolution(simple.sem.2)

##   lhs op rhs est.std    se     z pvalue
## 1   A  ~   L   0.589 0.026 23.07      0
## 2   L =~   B   1.000    NA    NA     NA
## 3   C  ~   L   0.638 0.024 26.19      0
## 4   B ~~   B   0.000    NA    NA     NA
## 5   A ~~   A   0.653 0.029 22.36      0
## 6   C ~~   C   0.593 0.027 22.36      0
## 7   L ~~   L   1.000 0.045 22.36      0
## 8   A ~~   C   0.384 0.027 14.27      0

messages.subject: Re: Difference between "regression" (~) and "Manifestation" (=~)
parts:
Ignore that last part about A~~D.  In my original example I have put the A ~ L link the wrong way round, it should be L ~ A and then the A~~D link doesn't appear in either, and when extended as Sing-Hang did you get the same result regardless of choosing =~ or ~ to express it.
 
So this seems to be a couple of things:
  •  sem fills out the model for you differently depending on whether you specify ~ or =~
  •  Something odd happens if you only specify one factor relationship
 
I also notice that you get an error if you try to define a latent variable relationship using only ~
